title: Optic: the system as built in the second round
subtitle: One application and its files on a volume, behind one password on the private test site; figures from the owner's own market feeds and the SEC, Milo's answers from Anthropic
source: github.com/sidprobstein/optic, branch factory/pass-2-works-data-workspace at 34a30b7; the test site's hosting record; read 2026-11-18

bands.label: The way in
bands.note: one password on the test site

nodes.title: A reader
nodes.desc: Someone who follows or owns stocks. Most of Optic works signed out; Milo, saved layouts and passkeys need a free account.

nodes.title: The owner
nodes.desc: The account named in ADMIN_EMAILS, with that address confirmed. Reads the Metrics page; billing is switched on by the owner's own variables later.

nodes.title: The password gate
nodes.desc: A Caddy reverse proxy with one basic-auth identity in front of the whole test site. It comes off at going live; the owner's public site has no gate.
notes: The password lives in the gate service's own variables, never in a file.

nodes.title: Home and its panels
nodes.desc: Home's panels in Blue, Gold and Teal link groups; named layouts saved on the account; the Optic Desk with its right column (sources, saved research, Milo follow-ups); ticker rows with today's line.

nodes.title: A company's pages
nodes.desc: The stock page's tabs keep the ticker and the place; Financials draws revenue, margins, cash flow and the balance sheet by year and quarter, each chart with its source line; the company grid opens by 'Open as panels'.

nodes.title: Ask Milo
nodes.desc: Ask Milo from any screen; the chart pressed or nearest the top on Financials and the timeframe on Chart go with the question. Reported figures in the answer are underlined with their source.

nodes.title: One look for every state
nodes.desc: Every panel the eight workflows cross draws loading, empty, stale and failed through one shared piece, with a retry where one helps.

nodes.title: Pages and figures
nodes.sub: each with its source and time
nodes.desc: Serves the page and the figures behind it; every figure carries the source it came from and its time.

nodes.title: Today's lines
nodes.desc: Up to thirty tickers' five-minute bars since the open in one answer, red or green by the day's direction, delayed or closed said plainly; the 30-session line when the market is shut. A licensed feed is one class here.

nodes.title: Insider history
nodes.desc: The free feed's latest insider rows and, before them, open-market purchases and sales read from SEC Form 4 filings, each linked to its filing.

nodes.title: Milo's answers
nodes.desc: Takes the question with the screen's figures, the reader's level and what is in view (checked and capped), checks the plan's allowance and streams the answer. Deep research reads live web sources. Records a question asked, never its text.

nodes.title: Saved layouts
nodes.desc: Named layouts kept on the reader's account: at most 20, names to 40 characters, each under 32 KB; only the owner of a layout reads or changes it. Built with an owner kind so a group can own one later.

nodes.title: Sign-in
nodes.desc: Sign-up, sign-in, confirmation, reset and passkeys, unchanged in shape; passkeys were tested end to end on the test site this round.

nodes.title: The three signals
nodes.desc: A stock opened from Home, a question to Milo and a visit, recorded with nothing personal and shown as raw counts to the confirmed owner.

nodes.title: SEC reader
nodes.desc: When the free feed's list stops short, one background reader fetches the missing Form 4 filings, a few a run and politely spaced, and keeps each one; the table fills in as it reads.

nodes.title: Watches and alerts
nodes.desc: The watch runs during market hours and the alerts they raise, shown in the app. Email delivery is wired and off on the test site: as built it sends one digest to one configured address.

nodes.title: Accounts file
nodes.desc: SQLite on the volume: accounts, sessions, passkeys, the Milo allowance, saved layouts (new this round, migration 22) and the usage signals.
nodes.evidence: app/db.py (MIGRATION 22 workspace_layouts); hosting record, volume at /app/data

nodes.title: Filings and caches
nodes.desc: The Form 4 filings already read (a filing never changes once accepted), the market caches and the paper ledger, on the same volume.

nodes.title: The owner's market feeds
nodes.desc: Yahoo Finance and the other feeds in the owner's code, labelled delayed. They are not licensed for showing to paying users; licensed data is a later round.

nodes.title: SEC EDGAR
nodes.desc: The SEC's own filing lists and Form 4 filings, read with a declared contact and within its fair-access rate.

nodes.title: Anthropic
nodes.desc: Milo's answers are written by Anthropic's API. On the test site the key is one we set; at going live it is the owner's own key, in the owner's own account.

nodes.title: Mail sink
nodes.desc: Every email the test site sends (confirmations, resets) stops in a Mailpit inbox behind the same password. At going live the owner's mail relay takes its place.

nodes.title: Stripe
nodes.desc: The billing code reads the Stripe key and price from the deployment's variables. Nothing is set on the test site, so no plan, price or button shows anywhere. Several prices are a later round.

nodes.title: SnapTrade
nodes.desc: Brokerage linking is in the owner's code and not switched on here: no SnapTrade test keys exist yet, so the link itself could not be tried. The page says so and offers the watchlist and the Paper Desk.

nodes.title: Alert email
nodes.desc: Alert email is off on the test site. As built it would send one digest to one configured address, not to each reader who set an alert; who should receive it is an open question for the owner.

edges.label: a question asked, never its text

traces.name: Milo is told the chart in view
traces.summary: A chart pressed on Financials, a question, and an answer about that chart.

steps.note: A reader on Apple's Financials, by quarter, presses Cash flow by quarter.
Ask Milo opens, and the chart pressed goes with the question, even though the panel moved the page.
The question goes to Optic through the password on the private site.
Milo checks the allowance and what is in view.
The answer is written about that chart and streams back, its reported figures underlined with their source.
A question asked is counted for the owner; its words are never kept.

traces.name: The full insider history from the SEC
traces.summary: From a press on 10 years to rows read from Form 4 filings.

steps.note: The reader opens Insider trades, full history, and presses 10 years.
The page asks for ten years of open-market purchases and sales.
Optic answers at once with what it already has.
Filings read before come from the store.
If filings are still unread, one reader starts in the background.
It reads the missing Form 4 filings from the SEC, newest first, politely spaced.
Each one is kept, and the table fills in as the reader comes back.

traces.name: A layout saved, opened from another browser
traces.summary: Link groups arranged, named, saved on the account, opened elsewhere.

steps.note: The reader puts panels into Blue, Gold and Teal groups and names the layout.
Save sends the layout's shape, nothing else.
Optic checks it is the reader's own, within the limits.
It is kept on the account, so any browser signed in can open it.

traces.name: Today's line on every ticker row
traces.summary: One request for every row, refreshed through the session.

steps.note: The reader opens Home during the session.
The page asks once for every ticker row.
Optic answers for all of them together, every five minutes while the market is open.
Five-minute bars since the open, labelled delayed; after the close, the last 30 sessions.
